- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 3-day average), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and recent price is volatile; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to capture mean reversion toward higher range.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 2–5 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is bullish or 1–3 days back if bearish.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.27–0.53) and price is consolidating, model tends to overpredict; apply downward correction of 0.5–2% to avoid false breakout signals.
